events.name: What's Your Name
events.intro: A gate in a wall. Rain. A Grunt on a deckchair under half an umbrella. "Yo. You the respectful one? Go on in. ...Hey. You ate?" It's the first thing anyone says. At the fountain, where there's taro: "You ate?" On the Shady House steps: "You ate?" The Shady House: a chandelier on the floor, a throne made from a sun lounger. Guzma: "So you're the one. Beat my boys and didn't rub it in. Huh." He looks you over. Guzma: "What's your name." You say it. Guzma: "A'ight. That's it. That's the interview. You're in. Number One Numbskull; I just made it up; it's the top one."

success.text: A villa. A bunk bed with the price tag still on. A lamp: ₽12,000, REDUCED.

events.name: The Villa
events.intro: Koa Ridgeway, on the top bunk, in the dark: Koa: "He ask your name?" Koa: "Three times I took it. Melemele. Third time, the captain didn't even watch. He was talking to somebody. Just said 'next.' I can tell you the day. I can tell you what I had for breakfast." Koa: "You know what Guzma said, when I showed up here? Soaking. He said, 'What's your name.' That's it. That's the whole reason. Nobody on that island'd used it in a month; I was 'the Ridgeway kid, shame about him.'"

success.text: Koa: "Walk back up there? Past all of 'em? ...If somebody was watchin'. Actually watchin'. I'd— nah. Who's gonna watch."
Koa: "Malasada. Two. Mum made 'em. She said, 'For luck.'" He's quiet a while. Koa: "Didn't work."
Koa: "Loud. He's got forty kids and he don't know what to do with us except be loud at everybody else. It works. Nobody calls us failures to our face."

success.text: You wash your own. That night, a bandana on your bunk. The skull on it's a bit wonky.

events.name: Get Well.
events.intro: A dock. Everything white. A lift that makes no noise. Wicke: "Welcome. You'll be in the conservation wing. I'm so sorry about the forms; there are eleven. I've filled in what I could." A poster, by the lift. A Pikachu, mid-leap. GET WELL. Under it: 98% RECOVERY RATE. The President's office: a woman arranging white flowers. Lusamine: "So you're the one with the gift. Come into the light. ...Yes. Your Pokémon look at you. Did you know that? Most people's don't. I notice things that look at one." Lusamine: "I'll call you Deputy. I've wanted a deputy. Faba's so eager. You're restful."

success.text: The staff floor. A white room. Two beds, made with corners.

events.name: The Staff Floor
events.intro: Zia Pemberton, a keeper, taking off white gloves a finger at a time: Zia: "I'm conservation. Third year. We do extraordinary work; I mean that. A Mareanie came in last month with half its spines gone. I've got it eating from my hand." Zia: "We've a ninety-eight per cent recovery rate. It's on the poster. D'you know what our release rate is? I looked. It isn't on the poster."

success.text: Zia: "Two. Per cent. I thought I'd misread. I ran it three ways."
She looks at the floor, which is white. Zia: "Downstairs. That's all anyone says. Downstairs."

Zia: "The Mareanie's better. It's been better for a fortnight. I wrote 'ready for release' on its chart. The next morning the chart said 'ready for preservation.' Somebody'd changed one word. In my handwriting. They're good; I'd not have known, but I never cross my t's."

events.name: The Wing
events.intro: The wing. Pools. Two hundred Pokémon, glossy, bright, well. It's the healthiest room in Alola. Curator Pua, gently, tidying a chart: "Aren't they lovely? It's for the best. Out there they'd only get hurt again."

choices.label: Walk to the back of the dock.

success.text: A rusted barge. A wheelhouse. Chalk on the wall, faded: two columns. And, propped behind a locker, a board with hand lettering: GET WELL. GO HOME. That night: a white uniform, and a pass. It opens every door but one.

success.text: It's the same Slowpoke. Aether hired Skull to steal it and sent its own people to save it. It wanted a theft on the news and a rescue on the poster.

events.name: The Corridor

Koa: "I been told to take it." The Slowpoke yawns. Lux, who was locked in a van: Lux: "Why's everybody got the same job?" Nobody asks how she got out.

success.text: The other squad's lead squares up.
The nursery's keeper: "Nobody's. It walked in. Two years back. It's got a friend here."

choices.label: "Put it down. All of us. See where it goes."

success.text: Four hands let go. It sits. It thinks about it. It takes about a minute. It's the longest minute in the corridor's history. It gets up. It goes back into the nursery, slowly, and lies down next to another Slowpoke, which shuffles over without waking. Both squads stand there. Koa: "...So nobody needed to steal it." Zia: "Nobody needed to have it." Uri: "I was told to take it." A pause. Uri: "I wasn't told what to do if it didn't want to go. Nobody's ever covered that." Lux: "It's got a friend." success.text: Aether Paradise, from below.

events.name: The Drain
events.intro: A drain under Aether Paradise. Dripping. A ladder up, and a door with frost on the handle.

success.text: It's colder at the top.

events.name: The Cold
events.intro: Rows of glass. Frost on the inside. A Pikachu, mid-leap. A Corsola. A Petilil. Each one bright, whole, at its best. Each with a label: PRESERVED AT ITS MOST BEAUTIFUL. Nothing's dead; they're in stasis, and can be woken. He's got the bat on his shoulder. He's not using it. Guzma: "She told me I was special. She said, 'You're my favourite broken thing.' I thought that was a nice thing to say. Nobody'd ever said 'favourite.'" Guzma: "Look at 'em. That's what she does with favourites."

success.text: He walks the row. He stops at an empty case, near the end. It's new. It's tall. It's about his height. Guzma: "...Nah."

events.name: Preserved
events.intro: The rows hum.

success.text: Curator Pua comes down the far stairs. "It's for the best," she says as she sends each one out.

success.text: The Pikachu. Guzma lifts the case lid. Guzma: "It was jumpin'. She froze it jumpin'." He carries it inside his jacket.

events.name: Second
events.intro: A porch light. A woman who's been expecting a knock for six years, answering one. Guzma's mother: "He's upstairs. He comes sometimes, when his father's out. I leave the back door. I've not moved anything." A boy's room. A shelf. Trophies, a dozen. Every one's silver. In the hall, a rack of golf clubs, each bent in the middle, the same way. Guzma, on a bed too short for him: Guzma: "Second. Second. Second. Old man kept 'em on the shelf so I'd see. Golf club's still in the hall." Guzma: "I passed, y'know. Every trial. They don't know that, back at the house; I let 'em think I washed out like them. I didn't wash out. I got to the end and Hala looked at me and looked at the other guy and picked the other guy." Guzma: "I ain't evil. I'm bad at it. I got forty kids in a wet house who failed a test some dead guy made up. I thought if I was scary enough, nobody'd call 'em failures. Then she comes along and she ain't scared of me at all. She thinks I'm cute. She says there's a fifth island and it needs a kahuna. I'd have done anything."

success.text: Guzma: "Plumes fed 'em. I yelled near 'em."
Guzma: "...'Boss.' Lux calls me 'big bro.' I told her to quit it." She hasn't.
He looks at the trophies a long time. Guzma: "...Yeah. Po Town. That's home, huh."

He's quiet. Guzma: "It was my height. I stood next to it. I ain't dumb. I'm her favourite. I seen what she does with favourites." A pause. Guzma: "I'm still gonna go. Tomorrow. If she calls. That's the messed-up part. I know what the case is for and I'm still gonna go, 'cause she's the only one ever picked me."

events.name: Under the Bed
events.intro: Under the bed: a Wimpod. It's been looking at the door for years. It sees him. It doesn't run. It's the only time a Wimpod doesn't run. Guzma: "...Lil' G. You're still— Ma's been feedin' you?"

success.text: You go down. His mother has made tea and doesn't ask. You're an Admin now, beside Plumeria.

success.text: At the door he says it, not looking: "Second. You're my second. Ain't a title I've had cause to give before." You're Guzma's Second.

events.name: Dead Heads
events.intro: A glass roof. White roses. A woman with scissors, cutting the brown ones off, dropping them in a basket. Lusamine: "Deputy. Hold this. ...One has to take them the moment they turn. Before they spoil the look of the others." Lusamine: "My husband went into one of those holes and didn't come out. The children grew. They changed. Everything I love leaves, or alters. I only want one thing to stay as it was. Is that monstrous? Every mother's wanted it." Lusamine: "The Beast doesn't change. It doesn't leave. It only wants. I understand it better than anyone I've met."

success.text: The scissors stop. Lusamine: "They aren't the ones I had." Then, quieter: Lusamine: "...I never met the ones they became. I was busy keeping the ones they'd been." Lusamine: "Deputy. You've never once tried to leave. I can't tell you what that means to me." She touches your collar. She straightens it. Lusamine: "I shan't ever let you." You are Branch Chief.

Lusamine: "Letting things go. He'd stand on the barge and wave. At a Corsola. As if it'd wave back." A pause. Lusamine: "It did, once. A branch. I've never forgiven it." Lusamine: "Deputy. Lusamine: "They're safe. Nothing can happen to them now. Do you know how rare that is? For a thing you love to be somewhere nothing can happen to it?" Lusamine: "Deputy. You've never once tried to leave. I can't tell you what that means to me." She touches your collar. She straightens it. Lusamine: "I shan't ever let you." You are Branch Chief.

She puts the scissors down. Carefully. In the basket, with the dead heads. Lusamine: "That was his. He lettered it. I kept the first half. It was the half that was true. They got well. The second half was— he went. The sign told everything to go, and then he went." A long time. Lusamine: "I couldn't have it on the wall saying that." Lusamine: "Deputy. You've never once tried to leave. I can't tell you what that means to me." She touches your collar. She straightens it. Lusamine: "I shan't ever let you." You are the President's Favourite.

events.name: Operation: The Bus Stop
events.intro: The order: shake down a bus stop on Route 8. "There's always somebody." Koa: "Always somebody here. Like, always. Old lady's been here every time we come. Three hours, sometimes." The old lady, Auntie Haunani: "It says ten past. It's said ten past since my husband was alive. It's never once been ten past."

success.text: She hands over her purse without looking at you. There's always somebody.

The timetable's behind cracked plastic. It's for a route that was changed nine years ago. "When does it actually come?" Auntie Haunani: "Twenty to. And only Tuesdays and Fridays. Everybody knows. You wait anyway, in case." You take it down. Koa's got a marker. Lux, who isn't meant to be here, has the best handwriting. A new one, on the back of a Po Town brochure: BUS: 20 TO. TUES + FRI. — SKULL. Auntie Haunani, reading it: "...Well. That's the first true thing that's been up there in nine years." She gets up. It's a Thursday. "I'll go home, then." There's nobody to shake down, after. That's why there always was.

A Grunt: "It ain't official. There's no captain. No stamp." "There's me. I'll watch." Each of the six takes the trial. You're the captain. The first is a boy who froze, once. He freezes.

success.text: The site isn't wrecked. In the morning, the real captain finds six sets of footprints and a gate that's been oiled. There's one tag. Small. By the stamp box: we came back.

events.name: Operation: Po Town Roof
events.intro: The order: guard the Shady House. All night. Guzma's expecting trouble. There are nine buckets on the landing. They're full. Plumeria: "He thinks somebody's comin' for him. Nobody's comin'. It's rained on that boy's bed for six years and he's put a guard on the door."

success.text: You stand at the door all night. Nobody comes. The buckets fill.

Tiles, tar, a ladder. The squad helps. It's raining throughout. Guzma, coming out at three in the morning, with a bat: Guzma: "What's that noise. Who's on my—" The Number One Numbskull, on his roof, with a hammer. Guzma: "...You're fixin' it." Guzma: "Nobody's ever—" He looks at the bat. He puts it down against the wall. Guzma: "You need somebody to hold the ladder?" He holds the ladder till it's done. The nine buckets are emptied. They're never needed again. He keeps one, by the bed. He doesn't say why.

failure.text: Tiles, tar, a ladder, and rain. You slip twice. Guzma comes out at three in the morning with a bat, sees you, and puts the bat down. Guzma: "You need somebody to hold the ladder?" He holds the ladder till it's done. The buckets are emptied. He keeps one, by the bed.

remembers.notice: Koa: "If I went back up there. You'd come?"
Koa: "Tupp says you're soft. I said yeah. So?"

events.name: Operation: The Intake
events.intro: The order: bring in six "rescues" from Melemele. Strays. Injured. "At risk."

success.text: Six crates, six forms. Uri signs them.

A Pikipek, "stray": it's on a wire outside a window; there's a dish on the sill. A Yungoos with a limp, "injured, unattended": a boy's two streets off, calling it. A Grubbin, "at risk": it's a Grubbin; it's fine. A Meowth with a bell, "stray": it's got a bell. A Wingull, oiled, "injured": it is; it needs the wing. A Slowpoke, "unusually placid": it's a Slowpoke. Uri: "I was told six." Zia: "You were told six rescues. That's one." Uri: "...I'll bring one. If I'm asked, I'll say there was one." A pause. Uri: "That's true, isn't it? It'd be the first time the form and the day matched." One Wingull comes in. Zia's got it flying in a week. It's the first chart she writes "ready for release" on.

events.name: Operation: The Poster
events.intro: The order: hang the new recovery poster at twelve Pokémon Centers. GET WELL. 98%.

success.text: Twelve Centers, twelve posters, straight.

choices.label: Write the release rate under it, in pencil.

success.text: The first Center. You hang it. Straight. Zia holds the tape. A pencil. Zia: "Small. So they have to come close." Under the 98%, in neat grey figures: released: 2%. By the third, somebody's found the first. A nurse, by telephone, to the Paradise: "There's a figure on your poster. Is it right? Because I've sent you forty this year and I've been telling their trainers 'soon.'" Wicke, taking the call: "I— one moment." She goes and looks. "It's right." At the twelfth Center, somebody's got there first. Under the pencil, in different pencil: where are the other 96? And under that, in a child's hand, a drawing of a Rockruff.

remembers.notice: Zia: "You read the chart before the patient. Good. No: bad. Read the patient."
Zia: "Faba's asked for your pass logs. I've given him mine instead. They're very dull."

events.name: Operation: The Cold Room
events.intro: The order: log the day's "preservations." Three. Sign. Lock up. B2. The frost. Three new cases, empty, humming, ready. Three trolleys. A Mareanie, glossy, every spine back. A Wingull. A Petilil. Each with a chart. Each chart on the wrong form. Curator Pua: "It's for the best. It is. They're perfect. They'll never be more— oh, that one's looking at me. They don't usually look." The log: three lines. You write them.

success.text: They're cased. Zia doesn't speak at supper.

choices.label: "Preserved." Three times, and don't close the cases.

success.text: The log says it. The room doesn't. Pua sees. She says nothing. It's for the best.
It's true. Wicke's lost the forms. Pua: "Is that— can one write that?" "It's what happened." Pua: "...I've never written what happened. I've written what was for the best." She initials it.

remembers.notice: Zia: "If I'm ever at my best, don't let anyone write it down."

events.name: The Cold Room
events.intro: And the door. A latch. It can be left.

success.text: It's the only door on B2 that's ever been left. That night, something small comes up the stairs from below, with its helmet off, and sits outside it. It's not waiting for orders. Whatever happens, nobody will need a key.
You lock up. The key goes back on its hook.

events.name: You Ate?
events.intro: Supper. Plumeria counts heads. Lux isn't there. She's under the table.

success.text: You eat. You wash your own bowl.

events.name: You Ate?
events.intro: Supper. Plumeria counts heads. Kimo isn't there. He's at the Ten-Coin Center, with a Grunt's Zubat in a sling. Plumeria takes his bowl over herself.

success.text: You eat. You wash your own bowl.

events.name: You Ate?
events.intro: Supper. Plumeria counts heads. Guzma isn't there. He's eaten, he says. He's on the roof.

success.text: He eats it. Guzma: "Don't tell Plumes." She can see you both from the kitchen.
You eat. You wash your own bowl.

events.name: You Ate?
events.intro: Supper. Plumeria counts heads. Nobody's missing. Plumeria: "Forty-one. Huh." She counts again. Plumeria: "First time in a year."

success.text: You eat. You wash your own bowl.

events.name: You Ate?
events.intro: Supper. Plumeria counts heads. Plumeria isn't there. She's dished up forty-one and she's on the step in the rain with the book.

success.text: She looks up. Nobody's ever said it back.
You leave her with the book.

events.name: Rounds
events.intro: The wing, at night. Zia does rounds. You carry the clipboard. The Mareanie. "Eating. Spines at 60%." Zia: "Another fortnight. Then I'll write 'ready.' I'm going to write it very clearly."

success.text: On to the next pool.

remembers.notice: Zia: "Don't let her call you that. I've seen where she keeps her favourites."

events.name: Rounds
events.intro: The wing, at night. Zia does rounds. You carry the clipboard. The Mareanie. "Ready for release." In her hand, t's crossed, underlined. Zia: "There. Let them change that."

success.text: On to the next pool.

events.name: Rounds
events.intro: The wing, at night. Zia does rounds. You carry the clipboard. The Mareanie. "Ready for preservation." Zia: "They didn't change the word. They changed the form. It's a different sheet. Same clipboard." She takes it off. She folds it. She puts it in her glove.

success.text: On to the next pool.

events.name: Rounds
events.intro: The wing, at night. Zia does rounds. You carry the clipboard. No chart. The pool's there. The Mareanie's there. Zia: "It hasn't got one. If it hasn't got a chart, nobody can sign it. I've lost two hundred and six charts. Wicke's lost the forms. We've not discussed it."

success.text: On to the next pool.

events.name: Rounds
events.intro: The wing, at night. Zia does rounds. You carry the clipboard. A wall. Two columns, in chalk: IN. HOME. The second column's empty. Zia: "For tomorrow."

success.text: On to the next pool.

events.name: The Night Run
events.intro: The sales office. Two in the morning. Plumeria, with a ledger, and a Meowth held by the scruff, which has given up. Plumeria: "You're up. Good. You're comin'. You tell anybody and I'll deny it and they'll believe me." Plumeria: "Entry three-oh-eight. Meowth. 'Borrowed' off a porch in Malie by two of my geniuses on Tuesday. It's got a bell on. It's somebody's baby." A road. A porch. A light on upstairs. She sets it down on the mat. It looks at her. It looks at the door. Plumeria: "Go on." It scratches. A light. A voice: "Is that— MITTENS?" A door. A shriek. Plumeria's already behind the hedge. She's got the book out. She writes a date in the second column. Plumeria: "Three hundred and six back. Six to go."

success.text: Plumeria: "'Cause he needs to think we're bad. If we ain't bad, what are we? Forty kids in a wet house. He can't look at that straight."
Plumeria: "'Cause I gotta be able to. Look at it straight."
She turns the book so you can read it. Six lines without a second date. Plumeria: "Take one, if you want. By the scruff. To a doorstep. Nobody suspects this of Skull."

events.name: An Entry in the Book
events.intro: One of the six from the Borrow Book: a Pichu, taken from a market stall in Konikoni. You've got it by the scruff. It's given up.

success.text: You set it down on the mat. It looks at you. It looks at the door. It scratches. A light, a voice, a door. Plumeria writes a date in the second column when you tell her. Nobody suspects this of Skull.

events.name: As They Were
events.intro: The family floor. Two doors, side by side. Lusamine, with a key on a ribbon. Lusamine: "Deputy. I'd like you to see. I don't show people." The first room. A girl's. White. A bed made for someone four feet tall. On it, laid out: a dress, a hat, small white shoes. Fresh. Pressed. Lusamine: "I lay them out. Every morning. In case she comes down." She smooths the collar. Lusamine: "She's— there's a tall girl about the place who answers to the name. I'm polite to her." The second room. A boy's. A height chart on the door frame, in pencil. It stops at ten. Lusamine: "He was measured every birthday. Then he stopped coming to be measured." She holds out the hat. Lusamine: "Would you? I've a call. Just lay it straight. On the pillow."

success.text: It's on the pillow tomorrow, and every day.
She finds the bed bare. She doesn't shout. She takes it out and lays it down again. Lusamine: "Deputy. We don't tidy her."

choices.label: (Mark the door frame: a new line, higher, with today's date.)

success.text: A pencil's there, on the ledge, where it's been for six years. You mark where a boy of sixteen would come to. Lusamine, in the doorway, back from her call: Lusamine: "...What's that." "Where he is now." She comes and stands under it. It's above her eye. Lusamine: "He's taller than me?" A long time. Lusamine: "I'd not— I've been looking down, for him. All this time. I'd have walked straight past."

events.name: Plumeria, Alone
events.intro: Po Town's roof, in the rain. Plumeria: "I'm not their boss. I'm their big sister. Somebody's got to check they ate. Guzma checks they're scary. I check they ate. You tell me which matters."

success.text: She laughs. It stops. Plumeria: "...Nobody. Huh."
Plumeria: "They'd follow a bowl. I just carry it."
Plumeria: "Whatever's left. He waits till everyone's done. Thinks I don't see."

events.name: Gladion, Alone
events.intro: A motel. Type: Null, with its helmet half off. Gladion: "I took it and ran. From her. It was a weapon that failed, so she froze it. I'm with Skull because nobody here asks what I'm running from."

success.text: He looks at it a long time. Gladion: "No. It isn't. It eats cereal out of my hand."
Gladion: "...I've been calling it 'Null.' That's what the file said." A pause. Gladion: "That's not a name, is it. That's what she called it." He gives it one.
Gladion: "Tell her what? She'd only freeze it again. Or me."

events.name: Faba, Alone
events.intro: His office. Every certificate he's ever earned. Faba: "Branch Chief. The last line of defence. She's never once used my name without 'thank you, that will be all' after it."

success.text: Faba: "More? I'm Branch Chief." He says it as if it were a ceiling.
Faba: "Research. Real research. I was going to cure something. I forget what."
Faba: "...I've never asked." He looks at the cold room's key on its hook.

events.name: Wicke, Alone
events.intro: The conservation deck. She's feeding something that should've been released. Wicke: "I sign the intake forms. I've stopped signing the other ones. They pile up. Nobody's noticed. If nobody signs, nothing's 'preserved.' It's the only disobedience I'm capable of."

success.text: Wicke: "Two hundred and six. They're all still awake."
Wicke: "Oh, I couldn't. If they're with me, they're lost. If they're with you, they're stolen." She keeps them.
Wicke: "Is it? I've never been sure anything I did was."

events.name: The Loyalty Test
events.intro: Guzma: "Smash it. That statue. Captain's statue. C'mon. Show me you're one of us."

success.text: Guzma: "...Nah?" He looks at you. He looks at the statue. Guzma: "Huh. Nah." He doesn't press it.
It comes apart easier than you'd think. Guzma whoops. It doesn't feel like anything.
He lifts the bat. He doesn't. Guzma: "...Ain't his fault I came second."

remembers.notice: Koa: "G's gonna make you smash somethin'. Tell him to do it himself. He won't."

events.name: The Loyalty Test
events.intro: Lusamine: "Choose one for the cold room. Any. Whichever you think is at its loveliest."

success.text: Lusamine: "None? Nothing at all is lovely enough to keep?" She looks at you as if you'd said something cruel.

choices.label: (Point at a rose in her garden.)

success.text: She follows your finger. A white rose, just open. She laughs, delighted. Lusamine: "Yes. Oh, yes. You do understand." She cuts it herself.
She goes along the pools. She looks. She stops at the Mareanie a long time. She doesn't choose.

remembers.notice: Zia: "She'll ask you to choose one for the cold. Point at a rose."

events.name: Found Out
events.intro: The Shady House gate is shut when you come back, and Plumeria is standing in front of it with three Grunts who won't meet your eye. Plumeria: "Somebody's been talkin' to the cops. Nanu's got a sheet with your name on it. I ain't sayin' it's you. I'm sayin' you're goin' out the long way." You've been found out. The only way back outside is through them, with your own party, on worse ground than you'd have chosen.

success.text: They come at you two at once.

remembers.notice: Koa is by the gate. He catches your eye, and takes one step sideways, out of their line.

events.name: Found Out
events.intro: The lift stops between floors. When the doors open, Faba is waiting, with two Employees and a clipboard. Faba: "Deputy. The President is very hurt. I, on the other hand, am delighted." You've been found out. The only way back outside is through them, with your own party, on worse ground than you'd have chosen.

success.text: They come at you two at once.

remembers.notice: Zia is in the corridor behind them. She takes one step sideways, out of their line.
